The knowledge base

Five real InsureX product PDFs, one per category, mostly in Thai

Built from insurex.co.th and the partner product pages it links to: 5 documents, 152 searchable chunks

DocumentWhat is insideChunks
Health7 products (Easy E-Health, E-Health Mini, HB Plus, Prima Care…), benefit tables with up to 10 plans side by side68
Accident38 personal accident plans from 4 insurers, for kids, working age and seniors49
Savings3 savings plans: Easy E-Save 10/3, คุ้มมั่งมี 18/9, คุ้มออมสุข14
TravelCover, optional extras and 28 FAQ answers14
PetTIP Pet Lover plans S–XXL, conditions, exclusions, FAQ7

How the PDFs were made

  • The brief's PDFs were not supplied, so each category page on insurex.co.th became one PDF.
  • Pages that build their content in the browser were rendered with Playwright in Edge: "show more" clicked until every plan appeared, every FAQ opened.
  • Plan counts were checked against the site's own totals.
Why it matters: real catalogues are harder than clean sample text. Big tables, many products per file and Thai script all broke the first version.
InsureX · Test Case 23
Reading the documents

Three problems in the real PDFs, each found by testing and fixed in the loader

The PDF reader is where most of the accuracy is won or lost

1 · Thai text was broken

pypdf dropped tone marks and upper vowels:

เบี ย instead of เบี้ย (premium)

Fix: switched to PyMuPDF, and mapped legacy font glyphs (Unicode U+F700–F71A) back to standard Thai.

2 · Tables fell apart

Every table cell came out on its own line, so a premium lost its row and its plan.

รายปี 36,500 109,500 182,000 362,000

Fix: text that shares a baseline (within 3 pt) is joined, so a table row stays one line.

3 · Which product is this table for?

A health PDF holds 7 products, and a benefit table rarely repeats the product name. "แผน M 3,000" could be any of them.

Fix: every chunk is labelled "document › section", taken from the headings and carried across pages.
Result: English questions find Thai answers (multilingual bge-m3), and a benefit table stays linked to the right product. Each fix has its own unit test.

InsureX · Test Case 26
RAG precision

Similar is not the same as relevant, so every answer passes a check first

An off-topic question can still score high similarity against insurance text, so an LLM grader checks the passages before any answer

Contextualizerewrite follow-ups using memory, in Thai
Retrievetop 4 chunks, similarity ≥ 0.45
GradeLLM keeps only passages that directly answer
Rewrite + retryone new query if none survive
Refuse politely"not in the documents", suggests what is

Recorded: a product InsureX doesn't sell

Do you sell car insurance?

classify → contextualize → retrieve → grade → rewrite_query → retrieve → grade → not_found → update_memory

Sorry, I couldn't find this in the InsureX product documents, so I can't give a reliable answer. I can help with InsureX health, personal accident, savings, travel and pet insurance.

Rules that hold on every answer

  • No relevant passage → no answer. The graph, not the LLM, enforces it.
  • Every fact carries a [file, page] citation, shown as a source chip.
  • The retry counter lives in the state, so the cycle cannot loop forever.

Bonus 1 · Lead collection via MCP

Interest turns the chat into lead capture, and bad data never reaches the database

Details are collected over several turns; a wrong phone number is rejected by the tool and asked for again

  • Lead mode persists in the graph state, so a product question in the middle is answered and then the missing fields are asked again.
  • The LLM extracts only what the customer typed into a Pydantic model.
  • Validation is inside the MCP tool: Thai phone format (normalised to 0XXXXXXXXX), positive income, trimmed name. Any client gets the same rules.
  • Recorded demo: 3 leads saved, one after a rejected phone "12345".
InsureX · Test Case 2 · screenshot of the running app9
Bonus 2 · Session memory

Each customer gets a separate memory that survives restarts

LangGraph checkpointer in SQLite, with thread_id = session_id

Same session remembers

What's my name, and what did I ask about first?

Your name is Alice Wong, and you first asked about Prima Care plan M's coverage for room and board.

Another session knows nothing

What's my name? What did I ask you before?

I don't have any previous conversation history to reference.

Long chats stay cheap

  • The last 8 messages go to the LLM each turn.
  • After 12 messages, older ones are folded into a running summary (update_memory node); the last 6 stay word for word.
  • Deleting a chat erases its memory; saved leads stay as business records.
Survives a restart: the demo closes and re-creates the whole assistant, then Alice asks "Can you remind me what the room rate was?" and gets "The room rate for Prima Care plan M is up to 3,000 THB per day."

InsureX · Test Case 2 · python main.py eval · 2026-10-0511
Tuning

The chunk size was chosen by the test, not by a rule of thumb

A quick retrieval sweep over 13 settings picked the candidates; each then ran all 100 questions end to end

Questions right, by chunk size / overlap (characters)

  • 1000 / 150 scored best: 91/100 (77/85 answers, 14/15 refusals).
  • Smaller chunks scored lower. The likely reason: at about 1000 characters a benefit-table block stays in one chunk with its plan headings.
  • Overlap stays at about 15%, so a fact on a chunk boundary is whole in at least one chunk.
Principle: every change in this project was checked against the same 100 questions, so improvements are numbers, not impressions.
InsureX · Test Case 2 · logs/chunk_comparison.md12
Honest limits

The 9 misses are mostly table lookups, and each has a clear next step

Every failing question is listed in the presenter guide and in logs/eval_report.md

What goes wrong

  • Wrong column or row in a wide table, e.g. a premium read from the next plan or age band.
  • A number from a neighbouring field, e.g. the premium given when the fracture benefit was asked.
  • Over-cautious refusals on a waiting-period question whose answer was retrieved but not used.

What I would do next

  • Parse tables into rows (or a small SQL table) and let the agent query premiums directly.
  • Hybrid search (BM25 + vectors) and a reranker for exact plan names and numbers.
  • Grow the test set with the sales team's real questions and add an LLM judge for answer quality.
Safety holds even when it misses: wrong cells are the risk, not invented products, and refusals for unknown products held 14/15.
